Title: One-shot design of functional protein binders with BindCraft
Authors: Martin Pacesa; Lennart Nickel; Christian Schellhaas; Joseph Schmidt; Ekaterina Pyatova; Lucas Kissling; Patrick Barendse; Jagrity Choudhury; Srajan Kapoor; Ana Alcaraz-Serna; Yehlin Cho; Kourosh H. Ghamary; Laura Vinué; Brahm J. Yachnin; Andrew M. Wollacott; Stephen Buckley; Adrie H. Westphal; Simon Lindhoud; Sandrine Georgeon; Casper A. Goverde; Georgios N. Hatzopoulos; Pierre Gönczy; Yannick D. Muller; Gerald Schwank; Daan C. Swarts; Alex J. Vecchio; Bernard L. Schneider; Sergey Ovchinnikov; Bruno E. Correia
Summary: BindCraft uses AlphaFold2-based optimization to design protein binders. Its experimental tests span cell-surface receptors, allergens, bacterial toxin targets and Cas9, with reported target-dependent success. It directly tests whether AI-designed binders can act on biological proteins without extensive screening.

Title: Accelerating protein engineering with fitness landscape modelling and reinforcement learning
Authors: Haoran Sun; Liang He; Pan Deng; Guoqing Liu; Zhiyu Zhao; Yuliang Jiang; Chuan Cao; Fusong Ju; Lijun Wu; Haiguang Liu; Tao Qin; Tie-Yan Liu
Summary: The μProtein framework combines a mutational-effect model with reinforcement learning to search protein fitness landscapes. Benchmarks and laboratory tests on β-lactamase show that single-mutation training data can guide the discovery of higher-function multi-mutation variants.

Title: Biophysics-based protein language models for protein engineering
Authors: Sam Gelman; Bryce Johnson; Chase R. Freschlin; Arnav Sharma; Sameer D’Costa; John Peters; Anthony Gitter; Philip A. Romero
Summary: METL pretrains a protein language model on biophysical simulations, then adapts it using experimental sequence–function data. It predicts properties including stability, catalytic activity and fluorescence, and designs functional GFP variants from a small training set. The study tests how physical knowledge can complement evolutionary sequence learning.

Title: Designer artificial environments for membrane protein synthesis
Authors: Conary Meyer; Alessandra Arizzi; Tanner Henson; Sharon Aviran; Marjorie L. Longo; Aijun Wang; Cheemeng Tan
Summary: MEMPLEX applies machine learning to experimental measurements of cell-free membrane-protein synthesis. It searches combinations of lipids, chemicals and chaperones across 28 membrane proteins and identifies conditions that synthesize previously difficult targets, connecting AI predictions to a practical biological production task.

Title: AMPGen: an evolutionary information-reserved and diffusion-driven generative model for de novo design of antimicrobial peptides
Authors: Shuwen Jin; Zihan Zeng; Xiyan Xiong; Baicheng Huang; Li Tang; Hongsheng Wang; Xiao Ma; Xiaochun Tang; Guoqing Shao; Xingxu Huang; Feng Lin
Summary: AMPGen uses a diffusion-based generative model and evolutionary sequence information to propose antimicrobial peptides. The authors synthesize and assay candidate peptides against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, testing biological activity rather than relying on computational scores alone.

Title: Design of highly functional genome editors by modelling CRISPR–Cas sequences
Authors: Jeffrey A. Ruffolo; Stephen Nayfach; Joseph Gallagher; Aadyot Bhatnagar; Joel Beazer; Riffat Hussain; Jordan Russ; Jennifer Yip; Emily Hill; Martin Pacesa; Alexander J. Meeske; Peter Cameron; Ali Madani
Summary: A biological language model trained on CRISPR-related sequences generates OpenCRISPR-1, an AI-designed genome editor. The study tests editing of human genomic targets, directly linking sequence generation with functional genome editing.

Title: Custom CRISPR–Cas9 PAM variants via scalable engineering and machine learning
Authors: Rachel A. Silverstein; Nahye Kim; Ann-Sophie Kroell; Russell T. Walton; Justin Delano; Rossano M. Butcher; Martin Pacesa; Blaire K. Smith; Kathleen A. Christie; Leillani L. Ha; Ronald J. Meis; Aaron B. Clark; Aviv D. Spinner; Cicera R. Lazzarotto; Yichao Li; Azusa Matsubara; Elizabeth O. Urbina; Gary A. Dahl; Bruno E. Correia; Debora S. Marks; Shengdar Q. Tsai; Luca Pinello; Suk See De Ravin; Qin Liu; Benjamin P. Kleinstiver
Summary: PAMmla learns the relationship between engineered Cas9 protein sequence and DNA target-recognition specificity from a large experimental screen. The authors use predictions to identify custom Cas9 variants and test editing activity and off-target effects in biological systems.

Title: Precise, predictable genome integrations by deep-learning-assisted design of microhomology-based templates
Authors: Thomas Naert; Taiyo Yamamoto; Shuting Han; Ruth Röck; Melanie Horn; Philipp Bethge; Nikita Vladimirov; Fabian F. Voigt; Joana Figueiro-Silva; Ruxandra Bachmann-Gagescu; Kris Vleminckx; Fritjof Helmchen; Soeren S. Lienkamp
Summary: Deep-learning predictions of DNA repair outcomes guide the design of microhomology-based templates for CRISPR-mediated genome integration. Experiments show improved frame-retaining insertion and fewer deletions, making this a direct application of AI to genome-engineering biology.

Title: Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome
Authors: Žiga Avsec; Natasha Latysheva; Jun Cheng; Guido Novati; Kyle R. Taylor; Tom Ward; Clare Bycroft; Lauren Nicolaisen; Eirini Arvaniti; Joshua Pan; Raina Thomas; Vincent Dutordoir; Matteo Perino; Soham De; Alexander Karollus; Adam Gayoso; Toby Sargeant; Anne Mottram; Lai Hong Wong; Pavol Drotár; Adam Kosiorek; Andrew Senior; Richard Tanburn; Taylor Applebaum; Souradeep Basu; Demis Hassabis; Pushmeet Kohli
Summary: AlphaGenome predicts many functional genomic measurements from long human and mouse DNA sequences at fine resolution. Its evaluation of regulatory variant effects addresses how AI can help interpret the biological consequences of noncoding sequence changes.

Title: Regulatory grammar in human promoters uncovered by MPRA-based deep learning
Authors: Lucía Barbadilla-Martínez; Noud Klaassen; Vinícius H. Franceschini-Santos; Jérémie Breda; Hatice Yücel; Miguel Hernández-Quiles; Tijs van Lieshout; Carlos G. Urzua Traslaviña; Minh Chau Luong Boi; Maryam Akbarzadeh; Celia Hermana-Garcia-Agullo; Sebastian Gregoricchio; Marcel de Haas; Roy Straver; Sarah Derks; Wilbert Zwart; Emile Voest; Lude Franke; Michiel Vermeulen; Jeroen de Ridder; Bas van Steensel
Summary: PARM combines massively parallel reporter assays with a deep-learning model of human promoter activity. It identifies regulatory sequence patterns and tests predictions about transcription-factor effects, directly studying the molecular grammar of gene regulation.

Title: Nicheformer: a foundation model for single-cell and spatial omics
Authors: Alejandro Tejada-Lapuerta; Anna C. Schaar; Robert Gutgesell; Giovanni Palla; Lennard Halle; Mariia Minaeva; Larsen Vornholz; Leander Dony; Francesca Drummer; Till Richter; Mojtaba Bahrami; Fabian J. Theis
Summary: Nicheformer trains on dissociated and spatial single-cell transcriptomic data from human and mouse tissues. It predicts spatial context for cells and compares with models trained without spatial information, showing how AI can represent tissue microenvironments.

Title: Mapping the topography of spatial gene expression with interpretable deep learning
Authors: Uthsav Chitra; Brian J. Arnold; Hirak Sarkar; Kohei Sanno; Cong Ma; Sereno Lopez-Darwin; Benjamin J. Raphael
Summary: GASTON uses an interpretable neural network to map spatial gene-expression gradients and tissue domains. Applications to brain and tumor tissue identify organized cell-state and expression patterns, making AI central to biological interpretation of spatial transcriptomic data.

Title: STAIG: Spatial transcriptomics analysis via image-aided graph contrastive learning for domain exploration and alignment-free integration
Authors: Yitao Yang; Yang Cui; Xin Zeng; Yubo Zhang; Martin Loza; Sung-Joon Park; Kenta Nakai
Summary: STAIG integrates spatial transcriptomic measurements, location and histology images with graph contrastive learning. Tissue benchmarks and tumor-microenvironment analyses test whether combining these modalities improves identification of spatial biological regions.

Title: STORIES: learning cell fate landscapes from spatial transcriptomics using optimal transport
Authors: Geert-Jan Huizing; Jules Samaran; Daniele Capocefalo; Anna Audit; Gabriel Peyré; Laura Cantini
Summary: STORIES models cell-fate trajectories from spatial transcriptomics across time using neural-network-based optimal transport. The authors evaluate developmental and regeneration atlases and recover known marker trends while proposing additional candidate drivers of cell differentiation.

Title: Learning cell dynamics with neural differential equations
Authors: Michael E. Vinyard; Anders W. Rasmussen; Ruitong Li; Allon M. Klein; Gad Getz; Luca Pinello
Summary: scDiffEq applies neural differential equations to single-cell profiles to infer cellular dynamics. Its evaluations include cell-fate prediction and analysis of differentiation, addressing the challenge of extracting temporal biological behavior from snapshot cell measurements.

Title: A digital twin for real-time biodiversity forecasting with citizen science data
Authors: Otso Ovaskainen; Steven Winter; Gleb Tikhonov; Patrik Lauha; Ari Lehtiö; Ossi Nokelainen; Nerea Abrego; Anni Aroluoma; Jesse Patrick Harrison; Mikko Heikkinen; Aleksi Kallio; Anniina Koliseva; Aleksi Lehikoinen; Tomas Roslin; Panu Somervuo; Allan Tainá Souza; Jemal Tahir; Jussi Talaskivi; Alpo Turunen; Aurélie Vancraeyenest; Gabriela Zuquim; Hannu Autto; Jari Hänninen; Jasmin Inkinen; Outa Kalttopää; Janne Koskinen; Matti Kotakorpi; Kim Kuntze; John Loehr; Marko Mutanen; Mikko Oranen; Riku Paavola; Risto Renkonen; Pauliina Schiestl-Aalto; Mikko Sipilä; Maija Sujala; Janne Sundell; Saana Tepsa; Esa-Pekka Tuominen; Joni Uusitalo; Mikko Vallinmäki; Emma Vatka; Silja Veikkolainen; Phillip C. Watts; David Dunson
Summary: A continuously updated biodiversity model combines machine-learning bird-call classifications with citizen-science and long-term observations. Independent tests on Finnish bird data show improved spatiotemporal distribution predictions, demonstrating an AI-assisted ecological forecasting application.

Title: Predicting microbial community structure and temporal dynamics by using graph neural network models
Authors: Kasper Skytte Andersen; Kai Zhao; Alexander de Linde Agerskov; Christian Bro Sørensen; Trine Juhl Holmager; Marta Nierychlo; Miriam Peces; Chenjuan Guo; Per Halkjær Nielsen
Summary: Graph neural networks use historical abundance measurements to forecast microbial community dynamics in 24 Danish wastewater-treatment plants. Tests also include a gut-microbiome dataset, directly applying AI to the temporal behavior of biological communities.

Title: Common to rare transfer learning (CORAL) enables inference and prediction for a quarter million rare Malagasy arthropods
Authors: Otso Ovaskainen; Steven Winter; Gleb Tikhonov; Nerea Abrego; Sten Anslan; Jeremy R. deWaard; Stephanie L. deWaard; Brian L. Fisher; Brendan Furneaux; Bess Hardwick; Deirdre Kerdraon; Mikko Pentinsaari; Dimby Raharinjanahary; Eric Tsiriniaina Rajoelison; Sujeevan Ratnasingham; Panu Somervuo; Jayme E. Sones; Evgeny V. Zakharov; Paul D. N. Hebert; Tomas Roslin; David Dunson
Summary: CORAL transfers information from common species to improve inference for rare ones in large biodiversity surveys. It is evaluated on DNA metabarcoding data representing more than 255,000 Malagasy arthropod species, addressing a central sampling problem in ecology.

Title: Data Fusion for Integrative Species Identification using Deep Learning
Authors: Lara M Kösters; Kevin Karbstein; Martin Hofmann; Ladislav Hodač; Patrick Mäder; Jana Wäldchen
Summary: A deep-learning system combines DNA sequences and specimen images for species identification. Tests across four plant and animal datasets show that the fused inputs can improve classification, particularly where one data type alone fails to distinguish closely related species.

Title: DeepForestVision: Automated wildlife identification for camera traps of African tropical forests
Authors: Hugo Magaldi; Raphaël Cornette; John Justice Tibesigwa; Raymond Katumba; Harold Rugonge; Bala Amarasekaran; Naomi Anderson; Noémie Cappelle; Anabelle W. Cardoso; Daniel Cornélis; Tobias Deschner; Davy Fonteyn; Rosa M. Garriga; Peter van Lunteren; Xavier Rufray; Hadrien Vanthomme; Joeri A. Zwerts; Sabrina Krief
Summary: DeepForestVision classifies wildlife in African tropical-forest camera-trap photographs and videos. The authors train on multicountry field data and compare against existing classifiers, testing the practical value and limits of AI for biodiversity monitoring.
